release_notes: Server operations moved off the legacy PW workflow onto AWS, with jobs now submitted and monitored directly against the Slurm REST API and a CLI-based binary build pipeline for distribution. Forecast verification was retired in favor of routing evaluation through the new eval-mgr service, while calibration/validation tuning periods gained a full rework of start/end/gap time-control math, multi-file tuning-parameter uploads, and better gage/domain handling. The service also picked up a health-check endpoint, CSRF/reverse-proxy hardening, and a Python 3.12 upgrade.

The tuning tab was reworked with clearer date/gap validation, warning states for out-of-range times, and server-driven (rather than client-calculated) time controls. A new full-page CLI download experience replaced the old modal, forecast verification screens were removed, and job lists across evaluation/forecast/hindcast gained multi-select bulk actions and combined calibration/validation status displays. Numerous navigation, help-content, and log-viewer formatting fixes rounded out the release.

The forcing engine was updated for NHF 1.2.2 hydrofabric compatibility, including catchment ID handling and refreshed golden test data. Status/payload reporting was migrated to the shared EWTS package, MRMS extraction scripts were added for OCONUS domains, and Alaska/Hawaii cold-start handling was refined alongside a Python 3.12 upgrade and ESMF mesh-creation retry logic.

Operational run scripts now support concurrent multi-VPU execution and two-pass/extended AnA cycles with windowed warm-start handling. EcFlow was moved into a dedicated container with a new `ecf_task_mgr` package (with its own test suite) for task status tracking, and streamflow data-assimilation preprocessing (USGS, USACE, Environment Canada, RFC) was added along with automatic recovery and stale-data cleanup. The release automation script (`createRelease.sh`) was also extended for AWS/PW environment releases with a regression test.

Calibration manager builds now publish SIF containers to GHCR for AWS PCS compute nodes, and the manager was updated to work with the newly split evaluation packages. SFT became individually calibratable, nexus-removal support was added, and the base image moved to Bookworm with optional EWTS installation.

Fixes addressed WRF-layout NWM retrospective forcing reads, per-domain meteorological coordinate reference systems, and ESTOFS mesh connectivity for dates before 2023. Streamflow feature ID deduplication and CO-OPS outage detection were corrected, and the project moved to a Python 3.13-only build and type-checking baseline.

A new production pipeline maps NWM channel and reservoir outputs into standardized NetCDF products and integrates with the RTE workflow via a dedicated production manager. RFC reservoir data ingestion (FTP download, PI-XML parsing, timeseries generation) and USGS/USACE/Environment Canada/CADWR timeslice merging were added, with multi-VPU support and parameterized S3 paths.

The evaluation manager was refactored into two independently installable packages, nwm_metrics and nwm_eval, with a new Sphinx-based documentation site. CADWR/ENVCA gage support, quantile vs. absolute threshold configuration, and NHF 1.2.0 crosswalk generation were added.

A new STATUS log level and JSON 'Payload' messaging system were added across the C, C++, Fortran, and Python bindings, writing structured status updates to a dedicated payload file alongside standard logs. Deprecated lazy logger binding was removed, and standalone runs now default to stdout logging.

Partition file handling for forecast and hindcast runs was corrected, and the hindcast function gained an optional generator mode so callers (including nwm-rte) can consume built realizations directly. STATUS-level payload logging, SIGTERM handling, and a lakeout postprocessing fix were also added, alongside the AWS migration and Bookworm base image conversion.

New EA and UAT2 environments were stood up with a flattened environment layout and public URL support, and PCS lifecycle guards were added so tag updates no longer replace the live compute fleet. MFA and LDAP support were added for authentication, along with RDS access via NGWPC Workspaces and increased compute sizing for the Django service.

RFC reservoir data assimilation configuration was added (with non-RFC assimilation disabled), and state-save/checkpoint directories became independently configurable. T-Route lake output is now produced by default, soil-layer adapters were updated to four layers, output format became user-configurable, and Topmodel's water-table method switched to a deficit-based calculation.

Regionalization support was extended to the Alaska domain for NHF 1.2.0/1.2.2, and single-VPU runs are now supported independently of multi-VPU workflows. Formulation selection moved to an average-score method, and path resolution bugs involving mixed placeholders and environment variables were fixed.

A new hindcast workflow was added, including cold-start-from-saved-state support, alongside RFC reservoir data assimilation and configurable state-save/checkpoint directories with restart support. Default and regionalized VPU runs, NWM output postprocessing, and EWTS-based status log parsing were also added or refactored.

Fixed duplicate serialization of the wetting-front count and added additional memory safety checks during state deserialization.
Standalone stdout logging now matches the EWTS log format, with a default logger guaranteed to be configured.

Added a new total soil moisture content output and corrected units for upper-zone soil moisture and HRU area, in addition to adopting the Payload status feature.

Fixed grid-rank reporting and reverted an incorrect grid-to-scalar conversion, along with other BMI corrections and EWTS build compatibility.

Implemented save-state messaging and made wetting-front-adjacent state variables (uz, wind speed handling) serializable, and updated time-handling inputs to accept externally supplied simulation time. Includes Python 3.14 compatibility fixes.

Added reservoir data assimilation (including USBR and Great Lakes as a dedicated reservoir type) and a new diversion data-assimilation mechanism modeled on an Old River Control Structure test case. Waterbody indexing was migrated to an NHF-native lake ID scheme with widened 64-bit identifiers, virtual-flowpath waterbody routing was fixed, and the compute engine received a round of performance optimizations (vectorized plan construction, MC kernel tuning, geopackage load streamlining) along with a large batch of post-merge stabilization fixes.
EWTS logging now defaults to on, several method names were updated for consistency, and the module builds cleanly without EWTS when the symbol is unset.

The core engine gained full checkpoint restart support for NetCDF output (including catchment index and variable-definition reconstruction), 64-bit catchment/nexus IDs, and structured Payload/STATUS logging with a periodic heartbeat. The Dockerfile was reorganized around a single configurable EWTS build flag, Python exceptions are now caught to prevent crashes on destroyed objects, and several model submodule references (t-route, SAC-SMA, LASAM, topoflow-glacier) were advanced.
